# PCV system oil catch can install

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

Mount an aftermarket oil catch can near the driver-side brake master cylinder and secure it with a hose clamp. [t337]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Mount an aftermarket oil catch can near the driver-side brake master cylinder using a bracket that holds the high-pressure AC line.
2. Secure the can to the bracket with a hose clamp and three zip-ties if drilling or modifying the original assembly is not desired.

_Procedure reported by [t337]._

## Tools

- [Partial] Hose clamp [t337]
- [Partial] Three zip-ties [t337]

## Parts

- Oil catch can [t337]
- PCV hose [t337]

## Tips & gotchas

- Position the can high enough to allow unscrewing the bottom half for easy emptying. [t337]
- Use a pinch-style hose clamp if standard clamps are too wide for the small PCV valve nozzle. [t337]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Drilling through the bracket or using holes in the firewall, which may require removing the entire assembly to service the can later. [t337]
